entries.title: Parity Multisig — initWallet hijack
entries.summary: Public initWallet on a deployed multisig allowed any caller to overwrite ownership and drain the wallet.
entries.root_cause: Initializer was not access-controlled and could be re-invoked after deployment.
entries.impact: Approximately 153,037 ETH drained from a single wallet.
entries.attacker_path: Call initWallet to overwrite owners, then withdraw wallet balance.
entries.invariant_broken: Wallet owners can be set only once, by the deployer.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed initWallet was bound to the constructor; deployment pattern made it post-callable.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker EOA ETH balance after attack > pre-attack balance + ~150,000 ether.
entries.victim_loss_check: Multisig wallet ETH balance after attack equals zero.
entries.audit_lesson: An initializer that is callable post-deployment is functionally an unowned setter for every state variable it touches. Treat 'init' on a deployed contract as a critical attack surface during review.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: this PoC is the canonical reference template. assertEq on pre/post balances and isOwner transition cover F1, F2, F4, F7. No further static-quality gaps; final promotion still requires archival fork verification.

entries.title: Parity Wallet Library — suicide
entries.summary: Anyone could initialize and then self-destruct the shared library that all Parity multisigs delegated to, freezing every dependent wallet.
entries.root_cause: Library contract had unprotected initialization and a privileged kill function reachable through delegatecall semantics.
entries.exploit_primitive: unprotected initialization plus self-destruct on shared library
entries.attacker_path: Initialize the shared library to take ownership, then call its kill function.
entries.invariant_broken: A shared library cannot be self-destructed by an unrelated caller.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed the library was permanently anchored by its consumers; nothing prevented direct ownership.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Library is selfdestructed; downstream wallet calls revert. (No direct attacker profit.)
entries.victim_loss_check: Library code at the well-known address is empty post-suicide; dependent wallets cannot delegatecall.
entries.notes: Phase 6C: additive assertions added — assertGt(code.length>0) before kill and assertEq(code.length==0) after kill, observing the pre-Cancun SELFDESTRUCT bytecode-clear fingerprint. Static proof target is now exact; runtime verification still pending an archival mainnet RPC at block 4501735 (public RPC returned 'historical state ... is not available' on 2026-05-22).

entries.title: BeautyChain (BEC) — batchTransfer overflow
entries.summary: Integer overflow in batchTransfer minted an arbitrary number of BEC tokens to attacker addresses, collapsing the token's market.
entries.root_cause: Unchecked multiplication of (count * value) in pre-0.8 Solidity allowed wraparound when both factors were large.
entries.impact: BEC token economically destroyed; trading halted on major exchanges.
entries.attacker_path: Call batchTransfer with crafted (count, value) pair that overflows count*value.
entries.invariant_broken: totalSupply equals sum of holder balances; transfers conserve supply.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed solidity arithmetic could not overflow at realistic input sizes.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker BEC balance after attack approximates the overflowed supply.
entries.victim_loss_check: Token totalSupply no longer matches sum of legitimate holder balances.
entries.notes: Phase 6D: additive assertions added — assertEq(a1After-a1Before, type(uint256).max/2+1), assertEq(a2After-a2Before, type(uint256).max/2+1), and assertGt(a1After+a2After, totalSupply()) capturing the canonical batchTransfer overflow fingerprint (count*value wraparound + invariant break). Static proof target is now exact; runtime verification still pending archival mainnet RPC at block 5483642 (public RPC returned 'historical state ... is not available' on 2026-05-22).

entries.title: SpankChain — payment channel reentrancy
entries.summary: Reentrancy in the payment-channel close path drained the SpankChain hub contract.
entries.root_cause: External call to a user-controlled token before state update in the channel close handler.
entries.impact: Approximately 165 ETH plus BOOTY balances drained.
entries.exploit_primitive: external token call before state update on channel close
entries.attacker_path: Open channel, trigger close path, reenter via ERC-20 token call before balance state is updated.
entries.invariant_broken: A channel close transfers exactly its remaining balance, once.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker ETH and BOOTY balances after attack > pre-attack + reentered withdrawals.
entries.victim_loss_check: SpankChain hub contract balance < pre-attack balance by the drained amount.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only inherited balanceLog modifier; no explicit asserts. The line `payable(address(0x0)).transfer(5 ether)` after the exploit burns the simulated flash-loan principal, which understates the After log. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot SpankChain hub ETH balance pre/post and assertLt; assert attacker net (before the burn) exceeds simulated principal.

entries.title: Uniswap V1 — imBTC reentrancy
entries.summary: ERC-777 transfer hook in imBTC enabled cross-function reentrancy against Uniswap V1's ETH→token swap path.
entries.root_cause: Uniswap V1 swap path performed external token transfer before updating internal reserves, and imBTC's ERC-777 _callTokensReceived gave the attacker control mid-execution.
entries.impact: Approximately 1,278 ETH and 24.5 imBTC drained from Uniswap pools.
entries.exploit_primitive: ERC-777 transfer hook re-entering Uniswap V1 swap path
entries.attacker_path: Initiate Uniswap V1 ETH->imBTC swap; reenter inside ERC-777 hook before reserves update.
entries.invariant_broken: Pool reserves are consistent with executed swaps when the next read occurs.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed ERC-20 transfers do not yield control to the recipient.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker ETH balance after attack > pre-attack balance plus drained pool ETH minus loan fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: Uniswap V1 pool ETH and imBTC reserves < pre-attack reserves by the drained amounts.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: PoC code targets Lendf.Me (IMoneyMarket supply/withdraw against `victim = 0x0eEe...`), not Uniswap V1. The cited PeckShield URL is the Uniswap+Lendf.Me joint analysis. Title kept for now to avoid id rename; reclassification deferred to a separate user-approved track. Assertions are absent — only emit log_named_uint. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot victim and attacker imBTC balances and assertLt / assertGt with the drained amount.
entries.latest_public_rpc_notes: Public Ethereum RPC failed during fork setup at vm.createSelectFork. Error: 'historical state is not available'. Exploit execution did not start; archival RPC required for verification.

entries.title: Bancor — public safeTransferFrom on newly deployed contract
entries.summary: A newly deployed Bancor contract exposed safeTransferFrom as a public function; any caller could move ERC-20 tokens that users had previously approved to that Bancor address.
entries.root_cause: Internal helper safeTransferFrom was left with public visibility on a deployed contract that already held outstanding user approvals.
entries.impact: Several users with active token approvals to the Bancor contract were drained; aggregate loss not authoritatively confirmed.

references.title: Example attack tx (cited in PoC source comment)

entries.exploit_primitive: public ERC-20 mover function on a contract holding live user approvals
entries.attacker_path: Identify a user who has approved the Bancor contract for an ERC-20, then call its public safeTransferFrom to move that user's tokens to the attacker.
entries.invariant_broken: Token approvals to a contract are spendable only by the contract's intended internal flows, not by arbitrary callers.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed the helper that consumes user approvals was internal; deployment exposed it as public.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker XBPToken balance after attack > pre-attack balance by the victim's drained amount.
entries.victim_loss_check: Victim XBPToken balance after attack equals zero (or pre-attack minus drained amount).
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: PoC code is the Bancor public-safeTransferFrom incident (June 2020), not the Balancer STA deflationary-token drain. Evidence: contract Exploit__202006 forks block 10307563 and calls IBancor(0x5f58058C0eC971492166763c8C22632B583F667f).safeTransferFrom(XBPToken=0x28dee0...,victim=0xfd0B4D...,attacker,victim_balance); source comment header reads 'Bancor Protocol Access Control Exploit PoC'. id slug retained to keep file paths stable; aggregate loss_usd intentionally absent pending manual confirmation. Protocol identity is high-confidence; status: needs-verification reflects archival fork run still pending. Phase 6E: additive assertions added in EVM/test/2020-06/Exploit_2020-06.t.sol (allowanceBefore >= victimBefore precondition; victimAfter == 0 and attackerAfter - attackerBefore == victimBefore postconditions). Patch compiles and forge fmt-clean; assertion logic unexecuted because public RPC returned 'historical state is not available' for block 10307563 — archival mainnet RPC required for execution. assertion_quality raised none→strong on static grounds; verification_status retained as not-run-no-rpc.

entries.title: Opyn — duplicate ETH option exercise
entries.summary: Opyn's exercise function summed msg.value across an array of options, letting one ETH payment exercise multiple option lots.
entries.root_cause: Loop over options used the single msg.value as collateral for each iteration instead of dividing it.
entries.impact: Approximately $370k of collateral drained from ETH put vaults.
entries.exploit_primitive: msg.value reused across array iterations in exercise
entries.attacker_path: Call exercise with multiple option lots so loop reuses single msg.value as collateral for each.
entries.invariant_broken: Each exercised option lot is collateralized by its own ETH payment.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed each option in the array independently bore its own collateral payment.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker collateral output > sum of legitimate per-option payments.
entries.victim_loss_check: Opyn vault collateral balance < pre-attack balance by the over-exercised amount.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only console.log of pre/post attacker USDC. The exploit calls opyn.exercise{value:30 ether} with two vaults (the attacker's and a real third party's), but the test never asserts the third-party vault collateral fell or that attacker USDC delta is positive. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot the second vault's collateral pre/post and assertLt; assertGt(balAfter, balBefore).

entries.title: bZx — iETH self-transfer double-write
entries.summary: bZx's iToken transfer logic let a holder transfer to themselves and double their iToken balance; in the PoC the targeted market is iETH (loanToken 0xB983E014...), which the attacker mints with ETH, self-transfers in a loop, then redeems with burnToEther.
entries.root_cause: _internalTransferFrom updated source then destination from cached pre-call balances, so when source equals destination the second write overwrote the first decrement, doubling the balance.
entries.impact: iETH market drained on the historical incident; aggregate cross-market loss not authoritatively re-confirmed from PoC code alone.
entries.exploit_primitive: self-transfer double-write in iToken accounting (iETH market)
entries.attacker_path: Mint iETH with ETH, repeatedly call iToken.transfer(self, balance) so the destination write overwrites the source decrement and doubles balance, then burnToEther to redeem ETH.
entries.invariant_broken: Internal token transfer preserves the sum of source and destination balances.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed source and destination of an internal transfer are different addresses.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker ETH balance after burnToEther > flash-loan principal (200 ether in PoC) plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: iETH loanToken contract underlying ETH balance < pre-attack balance by the duplicated redemption.
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: same root cause as the cited iUSDC incident, but the PoC targets iETH (loanToken=0xB983E01458529665007fF7E0CDdeCDB74B967Eb6, IETHv2/iETH on bZx) at fork block 10852715. attack_tx, attacker address, and the cited PeckShield URL are kept since the PoC source comment block names them; loss_usd retained from prior entry would be misleading for the iETH-only path the PoC executes, so it has been removed pending manual confirmation. Title and summary updated to reflect iETH; id slug retained to keep file paths and references stable. Phase 6F: additive assertions added in EVM/test/2020-09/Exploit_2020-09.t.sol — mintAmount captured from mintWithEther; per-iteration assertEq(balanceOf, expected) inside the existing 4-iteration loop with expected doubling each step (F6 fingerprint); final assertEq(balanceOf, mintAmount * 16); redeemed captured from burnToEther with assertGt(redeemed, 200 ether) F1 lower bound. Patch compiles and forge fmt-clean; assertion logic unexecuted because public RPC returned 'historical state is not available' for block 10852715 — archival mainnet RPC required for execution. assertion_quality raised weak→strong on static grounds; verification_status retained as not-run-no-rpc.

entries.title: Harvest Finance — fUSDT/fUSDC oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Flash-loan-funded swap on Curve Y-pool moved the spot price Harvest used to mint fTokens, letting the attacker mint cheap and redeem high.
entries.root_cause: Harvest derived share price from the same Curve pool the attacker could move with a single flash loan.
entries.impact: Approximately $33.8M drained from fUSDT and fUSDC vaults.
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, swap to imbalance Curve Y-pool, deposit into Harvest at distorted price, withdraw, reverse swap.
entries.invariant_broken: fToken share price reflects fair value of underlying, independent of intra-tx pool moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Curve spot price was a usable proxy for fair price within one transaction.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: fUSDT/fUSDC vault underlying balance < pre-attack balance.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only emit log_named_uint of attacker USDC/USDT pre/post. No strict profit assertion, no F2 victim assertion against fUSDC vault, no F5 oracle-deviation assertion against the manipulated Curve Y-pool spot price. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot fUSDC vault underlying pre/post and assertLt; assertGt(usdc.balanceOf(this), pre + flashloan_fees).

entries.title: Pickle Finance — swapExactJarForJar arbitrary-call drains cDAI strategy
entries.summary: Attacker called Pickle ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar with attacker-deployed FakeJar/FakeUnderlying contracts and CurveLogic-encoded arbitrary calldata, forcing the legitimate cDAI strategy to withdrawAll() and then redirect cDAI to tx.origin via the controller's permission set.
entries.root_cause: swapExactJarForJar accepted unvalidated jar/strategy targets and forwarded attacker-controlled calldata through CurveLogic.add_liquidity, letting the attacker invoke privileged strategy functions (withdrawAll, withdraw(address)) on the real pDAI strategy.
entries.impact: pDAI strategy cDAI position drained to attacker (tx.origin); historical incident reported around $19.7M for the broader Pickle Finance cDAI exploit.

references.title: samczsun reference exploit (linked from PoC source comment)

entries.exploit_primitive: controller route accepting unvalidated jar plus arbitrary external-call payload
entries.attacker_path: Deploy FakeJar/FakeUnderlying mocks; call ControllerV4.swapExactJarForJar(fakeJar, fakeJar, 0, 0, targets[], datas[]) where datas encode CurveLogic.add_liquidity wrapping STRAT.withdrawAll(), repeated PDAI.earn(), and STRAT.withdraw(address) — final step ships cDAI to tx.origin.
entries.invariant_broken: Controller routes only forward calldata to vetted jars/strategies, not arbitrary attacker contracts.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed swap-route targets and payloads were constrained to known jars/curves.
entries.attacker_profit_check: msg.sender (tx.origin) cDAI balance after exploit > pre-attack balance by drained pDAI strategy cDAI position.
entries.victim_loss_check: DAI/cDAI held by pDAI (0x6949Bb...) and its strategy (0xCd892a...) drops to (near) zero post-exploit.
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: PoC code is the Pickle Finance ControllerV4 swapExactJarForJar exploit (Nov 21 2020), not Cheese Bank's LP-oracle manipulation. Evidence: contract Exploit__202011 forks block 11303122 (not the prior 11205646), instantiates ControllerLike CONTROLLER=0x6847259b2B3A4c17e7c43C54409810aF48bA5210 (Pickle ControllerV4), JarLike PDAI=0x6949Bb624E8e8A90F87cD2058139fcd77D2F3F87, CurveLogic=0x6186E99D9CFb05E1Fdf1b442178806E81da21dD8, and STRAT=0xCd892a97951d46615484359355e3Ed88131f829D, then calls swapExactJarForJar with FakeJar/FakeUnderlying mocks. block_number, attack_tx, root_cause, impact, summary, references, category, protocol, and title all corrected. id slug retained to avoid file-path churn; aggregate loss_usd intentionally absent pending manual confirmation against the historical Pickle Finance incident.

entries.title: Cover Protocol — Blacksmith claimRewards infinite mint
entries.summary: Cover Protocol's Blacksmith staking contract miscalculated reward accounting on the BPT pool, letting a depositor claim a vastly inflated quantity of newly minted COVER tokens after a single deposit.
entries.root_cause: Reward accounting in Blacksmith allowed claimRewards to mint COVER from a stale or unbounded reward index for the BPT pool, breaking the link between staked balance, reward rate, and minted supply.
entries.impact: Effectively unbounded mint of COVER tokens against the staked BPT position; historical incident reported in the tens of millions before the white-hat reversal.

references.title: Cover Protocol Blacksmith contract (cited in PoC source)

entries.exploit_primitive: Blacksmith staking pool reward accounting allowing inflated claimRewards mint
entries.attacker_path: Deposit BPT (Balancer pool token 0x59686E01...) into Blacksmith (0xE0B94a7B...) via deposit(bpt, amount), then call claimRewards(bpt) — the bug mints an outsized COVER amount to the depositor.
entries.invariant_broken: Total COVER minted via Blacksmith equals the configured per-block reward rate times elapsed-blocks times pool-share.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Blacksmith's reward index was monotonic and bounded by the pool's accumulated rewards.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker (0x00007569...) COVER balance after claimRewards >> 0 and outside any normal staking yield bound.
entries.victim_loss_check: COVER token totalSupply increases far beyond the protocol's per-block emissions schedule; staking pool reward index inconsistent with cumulative emissions.
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: PoC code is the Cover Protocol Blacksmith claimRewards exploit (Dec 28 2020), not Warp Finance. Evidence: contract Exploit__202012 forks block 11542309, instantiates Blacksmith bs=0xE0B94a7BB45dD905c79bB1992C9879f40F1CAeD5, BPT=0x59686E01Aa841f622a43688153062C2f24F8fDed, COVER=0x5D8d9F5b96f4438195BE9b99eee6118Ed4304286, pranks 0x00007569... and calls bs.deposit(bpt, ...) followed by bs.claimRewards(bpt), then logs Cover.balanceOf(0x00007569...). Title, protocol, category, root_cause, summary, references, attack_tx, and loss_usd corrected; aggregate loss_usd intentionally absent pending manual confirmation. id slug retained to keep file paths stable.

entries.title: SushiSwap SushiMaker — DIGG/WBTC missing-bridge convert exploit
entries.summary: SushiMaker.convert performed an unguarded swap through a non-existent DIGG/WETH 'bridge'; an attacker created a thin DIGG/WETH pair, made the maker dump WBTC fees through the attacker pair at a controlled rate, and pulled the proceeds back to WETH.
entries.root_cause: SushiMaker burned LP fees and converted the resulting tokens to SUSHI via assumed bridge pairs, but DIGG/WBTC had no real bridge — convert(WBTC, DIGG) routed through any attacker-deployed DIGG/WETH pair without slippage protection.
entries.impact: Attacker captured the WBTC fee accumulated in SushiMaker for the DIGG/WBTC pair via a single thinly-funded fake pool; historical writeups attribute the proceeds to the attacker's WETH wallet.
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: PoC code is the SushiSwap SushiMaker missing-bridge exploit (Jan 26 2021), not Saddle Finance. Evidence: Exploit__202101 forks block 11720049, declares sushiMaker=0xE11fc0B43ab98Eb91e9836129d1ee7c3Bc95df50, sushiFactory=0xC0AEe478e3658e2610c5F7A4A2E1777cE9e4f2Ac, wbtc=0x2260FAC5...(WBTC), digg=0x798D1bE8...(DIGG), creates a fake DIGG/WETH pair, calls sushiMaker.convert(WBTC, DIGG), then redeems via removeLiquidity → WETH. Source comment cites Sushiswap SushiMaker.sol L192 and links to cmichel/slowmist/rekt postmortems. Title, protocol, category, root_cause, summary, references, exploit_primitive, attacker_path, profit/loss checks, and status replaced. id slug retained to avoid file-path churn; aggregate loss_usd intentionally absent pending manual confirmation.

references.title: cmichel — replaying Sushiswap / Badger / DIGG (referenced in PoC source comment)
rekt.news — Badger's DIGG / Sushi (referenced in PoC source comment)

entries.exploit_primitive: SushiMaker convert routing through attacker-provided thin pair due to missing bridge
entries.attacker_path: Wrap a tiny amount of ETH, swap WETH→WBTC→DIGG to seed liquidity, create a DIGG/WETH SushiSwap pair with the resulting tokens, call sushiMaker.convert(WBTC, DIGG) which dumps maker WBTC through the attacker pair, then withdraw LP and route the residual DIGG back to WETH.
entries.invariant_broken: SushiMaker.convert routes fee tokens only through bridges it controls or can price safely.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed every onsen-listed pair had a configured bridge in SushiMaker before convert was callable.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker WETH balance after rugPull > pre-attack WETH balance plus the 0.001 ether seed.
entries.victim_loss_check: WBTC fee balance held by SushiMaker (0xE11fc0B43ab98Eb91e9836129d1ee7c3Bc95df50) for the DIGG/WBTC pair drops to (near) zero post-convert.

entries.title: Yearn v1 DAI vault — Curve 3pool oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Attacker imbalanced the Curve 3pool around the yDAI vault's deposit and withdrawal calls, extracting value via the share-price difference.
entries.root_cause: Vault accounting depended on the spot virtual price of a Curve pool the attacker could push and pull with flash loans within one transaction.
entries.impact: Approximately $11M of DAI/USDC/USDT extracted from the yDAI vault.
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, imbalance Curve 3pool around yDAI deposit and withdraw, capture share-price delta.
entries.invariant_broken: yDAI share price reflects fair value of underlying, independent of intra-tx Curve moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Curve virtual-price was usable as oracle within one transaction.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: yDAI vault underlying balance < pre-attack balance.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: two require() lines actually fail the test if exploit math drifts (post-DAI == pre-DAI + 1, post-USDC == pre-USDC + 1), giving partial F1 coverage. No assertGt for crv3 / USDT profit and no F2 victim assertion against yvDAI total assets. Recommended Phase 6 patch: add assertGt(crv3.balanceOf(this), 0), assertGt(usdt.balanceOf(this), 0), and snapshot yvDAI underlying pre/post.

entries.title: DODO — CrowdPooling init reentrancy
entries.summary: DODO crowdpools could be re-initialized after the first init, letting the attacker repoint the pool at malicious tokens and drain liquidity.
entries.root_cause: init function lacked a guard against re-entry / re-initialization, and flash-loaned reserves left the legitimate state replaceable mid-call.
entries.exploit_primitive: re-initialization of crowdpool with attacker tokens
entries.attacker_path: Flash-loan reserves, call init again with attacker-controlled tokens, drain liquidity.
entries.invariant_broken: init runs exactly once and binds the pool's tokens for its lifetime.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed init was guarded against re-entry once liquidity was present.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker token balance after drain > attacker tokens supplied.
entries.victim_loss_check: Crowdpool reserves < pre-attack reserves; reserve token now attacker-controlled.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only emit log_named_uint of pre/post wCRES + USDT balances. No assertion that DVM was actually re-initialized with attacker tokens, and no strict profit assertion. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot DVM _BASE_TOKEN_ and _QUOTE_TOKEN_ pre/post and assert they changed; assertGt on attacker wCRES + USDT balances.

entries.title: Indexed Finance — DEFI5/CC10 reweight manipulation
entries.summary: During an index reweighting, the attacker swung weights with a flash loan such that a small input minted a disproportionate amount of index tokens, then redeemed the underlying basket.
entries.root_cause: Reweighting math allowed an attacker-supplied imbalance to dominate the new weights, breaking the invariant that the pool was worth its underlying basket during the transition.
entries.impact: Approximately $16M drained from DEFI5 and CC10 indices.
entries.attacker_path: Flash-loan supply, dominate reweight inputs, mint outsized index tokens, redeem underlying basket.
entries.invariant_broken: Index token mint price equals the fair basket value during reweighting.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed reweight inputs were bounded by realistic counterparty capital.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker basket-asset balance after redeem > pre-attack basket-asset balance.
entries.victim_loss_check: DEFI5 / CC10 underlying balances < pre-attack balances.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only console.log of final attacker token balances; no strict profit or invariant assertion. Recommended Phase 6 patch: snapshot pre-balances of all 8 borrowed tokens and after start() assert at least one assertGt with the documented attacker margin; assert DEFI5 underlying basket value (sum of pool token reserves * spot prices) dropped vs pre.

entries.title: BUILD Finance — governance takeover via low-quorum proposal
entries.summary: An attacker received 101.5 BUILD from a top holder, used it to submit a governance proposal that approved an attacker EOA on the BUILD token's governance contract, voted with another large holder's prank-pranked balance, warped past the timelock, executed the proposal, and then transferFrom'd the BuildGovernance treasury balance.
entries.root_cause: BUILD governance allowed proposals to grant arbitrary token approvals from the governance contract itself, with quorum/threshold parameters reachable by a small minority of token holders.
entries.impact: BuildGovernance treasury BUILD balance fully drained to attacker; historical incident reported around $470k.

references.title: BUILD Finance attack tx (cited in PoC source)

entries.exploit_primitive: minority-quorum governance proposal granting attacker an unlimited token approval on the governance contract
entries.attacker_path: Acquire BUILD via prank-from a top holder; propose a governance action that calls BUILD.approve(attacker, max) with msg.sender = BuildGovernance; vote with another whale balance; warp past timelock; execute; then BUILD.transferFrom(BuildGovernance, attacker, treasury_balance).
entries.invariant_broken: Governance proposals cannot move the protocol's own treasury without quorum from independent token holders.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed token-distribution made minority-quorum proposals economically unreachable.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker BUILD balance after exploit > pre-attack balance by the entire BuildGovernance treasury.
entries.victim_loss_check: BUILD token balance held by BuildGovernance (0x5A6eBeB6...) is zero post-execute.
entries.notes: Phase 6A reclassification: PoC code is the BUILD Finance governance takeover (Feb 2022), not Dexible. Evidence: Exploit__202202 forks block 14235712, instantiates BuildGovernance=0x5A6eBeB61A80B2a2a5e0B4D893D731358d888583 and BUILD token=0x6e36556B3ee5Aa28Def2a8EC3DAe30eC2B208739, pranks 0x562680a4... to receive BUILD, calls BuildGovernance.propose(BUILD, 0, approve(0xb4c79dab8f...,max)), votes via 0xf41c13f4..., warps to timestamp 1655436437, executes, then BUILD.transferFrom(BuildGovernance, this, balance). Title, protocol, category, root_cause, summary, references, exploit_primitive, attacker_path, profit/loss checks updated. id slug retained to keep paths stable; aggregate loss_usd intentionally absent pending manual confirmation.

entries.title: Moonwell — Chainlink oracle staleness on Base
entries.summary: Moonwell's price feed returned a stale value for a market on Base, letting an attacker borrow against inflated collateral.
entries.root_cause: Oracle wrapper did not enforce freshness against the underlying Chainlink answer's updatedAt timestamp under the conditions present at the attack block.
entries.impact: Approximately $1M extracted from a single market.
entries.exploit_primitive: stale Chainlink answer accepted at borrow time
entries.attacker_path: Borrow against a market while its Chainlink feed is returning a stale (favorable) price.
entries.invariant_broken: Borrow accounting reads only fresh oracle prices.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Chainlink answers were always fresh enough for instantaneous use.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker borrowed-asset balance > borrow input value at fair price.
entries.victim_loss_check: Moonwell market collateral / reserves < pre-attack balance.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: single assertGt(wethAfter, wethBefore) covers F1 attacker profit. Missing F5 oracle-deviation assertion (no read of Chainlink latestRoundData updatedAt vs block.timestamp) and missing F2 victim assertion against Moonwell market cash. Recommended Phase 6 patch: capture mwstEth cash pre/post and assertLt by BORROW_AMOUNT; read the underlying Chainlink feed and assert updatedAt < block.timestamp - heartbeat.

entries.title: yETH — pool invariant manipulation
entries.summary: A multi-phase sequence of add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, rate updates, and an OETH rebase manipulated the yETH pool's vb_prod_sum invariant, ending with a full pool drain.
entries.root_cause: yETH's stable-swap-style invariant could be steered through a specific sequence of liquidity moves and rate updates, breaking the relationship between LP supply and underlying assets.
entries.impact: Approximately $9M drained from the yETH pool.
entries.exploit_primitive: multi-step liquidity / rate / rebase sequence steering pool invariant
entries.attacker_path: Sequence add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, rate updates, OETH rebase to steer vb_prod_sum, then drain.
entries.invariant_broken: yETH pool invariant is preserved across any sequence of valid liquidity moves and rate updates.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed every reachable sequence of liquidity moves and rate updates left the pool's value-conservation invariant intact.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker pool-asset balance after sequence > pre-attack balance.
entries.notes: Phase 5 static review: only console.log of vb_prod_sum and inherited balanceLog. The _takeInitialsBack helper rebases attacker balances via deal(), which can mask whether profit was real. Recommended Phase 6 patch: after final drain, assert IERC20(POOL.assets(i)).balanceOf(POOL) <= dust for each of the 8 assets; before the bookkeeping rebase, assert attacker balance > pre-balance for at least one underlying asset.
